title: Windows Update Stack Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: CVSS AV:L/PR:L/UI:N; reducing untrusted local execution may reduce opportunity but no exact Microsoft workaround is documented.
Microsoft marks exploitation detected; generic EDR may limit impact but receives no likelihood credit.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') in Windows Update Stack allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can execute code in a low-privilege AppContainer could exploit this vulnerability locally to escape the sandbox and elevate privileges on the affected system. No additional user interaction is required.

title: Microsoft SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: CVSS AV:N/PR:N/UI:R; network ACLs reduce reachable senders, although the vector still requires user interaction.
Application control may limit post-exploitation impact; no exact Microsoft workaround or content-delivery path is established.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component ('injection') in SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to submit specially crafted instructions to SQL Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio. Successful exploitation could bypass intended read-only restrictions and allow database data to be accessed or modified using the connected user's permissions. User interaction is required.

notes.value: External control of file name or path in Skype for Business allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability over the network by sending a specially crafted request that writes an attacker-controlled file to an arbitrary location on the affected server. Successful exploitation could result in the attacker executing code on the target server. No authentication or user interaction is required.

title: Microsoft Office Outlook Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

products.name: Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise for 32-bit Systems
Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise for 64-bit Systems

mitigation_candidates.evidence: CVSS AV:N/PR:N/UI:N; network controls may reduce reachability, but no MSRC text supports an email or Protected View path.
Application control may constrain post-exploitation execution; it receives no likelihood credit.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could send a specially crafted email message to a target user. Simply viewing the message in the Outlook Reading Pane could trigger the vulnerability, without the recipient opening the message or clicking anything in it. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the recipient's system. Network access is required; authentication and user interaction are not required.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:

The security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 are not immediately available. The updates will be released as soon as possible, and when they are available, customers will be notified via a revision to this CVE information.
